'''Roy Lee Adler''' (February 22, 1931 – July 26, 2016<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?pid=180817333|title=Roy Adler Obituary - Mount Kisco, NY|work=The New York Times|date=July 29, 2016|access-date=2 December 2016}}</ref>) was an American mathematician.

Adler earned his Ph.D. in 1961 from [[Yale University]] under the supervision of [[Shizuo Kakutani]] (''On some algebraic aspects of measure preserving transformations'').<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=9153 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> He then worked as a mathematician for IBM at the [[Thomas J. Watson Research Center]].

Adler studies [[dynamical system]]s, [[ergodic theory]], [[symbolic dynamics|symbolic]] and [[topological dynamics]] and [[coding theory]]. The [[road coloring problem]] that was solved by [[Avraham Trakhtman]] in 2007 came from him, along with [[L. W. Goodwyn]] and [[Benjamin Weiss]].

He was a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-11-24.</ref> A paper was written on his work and the impact of his work by Bruce Kitchens and others.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kitchens|first1=Bruce|last2=Marcus|first2=Brian|last3=Weiss|first3=Benjamin|last4=Department of Mathematical Sciences, Indiana University Purdue University Indianapolis, Indianapolis, IN 46202, USA|last5=Department of Mathematics, University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC, V6T 1Z2, Canada|last6=Einstein Institute of Mathematics, Edmond J. Safra Campus, Givat Ram, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem 91904, Israel|date=2018|title=Roy Adler and the lasting impact of his work|journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics|language=en|volume=13|issue=1|pages=v–x|doi=10.3934/jmd.2018v|issn=1930-532X|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Writings ==
*With [[Brian Marcus]]: ''Topological entropy and equivalence of dynamical systems''. Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society. '''20''' (1979), no 219.
*With [[Benjamin Weiss]]: ''Similarity of automorphisms of the torus'', Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society (1970), no 98.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Adler|first=Roy L.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GDjfSAAACAAJ|title=Similarity of Automorphisms of the Torus by Roy L. Adler and Benjamin Weiss|date=1970|publisher=American Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref>
*[https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1998-35-01/S0273-0979-98-00737-X/ ''Symbolic dynamics and Markov partitions''], Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society. '''35''' (1998), no 1, 1–57.
*With L. Wayne Goodwyn and Benjamin Weiss: [https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02761605 ''Equivalence of topological Markov shifts''], [[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]. '''27''' (1977), 49–63.
*With [[Alan Konheim]] and M. H. McAndrew: ''Topological Entropy'', Transactions of the American Mathematical Society. '''114''' (1965), 309–319.
*With Tomasz Downarowicz and [[Michał Misiurewicz]]: [http://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Topological_entropy Topological Entropy]. Scholarpedia. '''3''' (2008), no 2, 2200.
*With Charles Tresser and Patrick A. Worfolk: ''Topological conjugacy of linear endomorphisms of the 2-torus'', Transactions of the American Mathematical Society. '''349''' (1997), 1633–1652.
*With Benjamin Weiss: ''Entropy, a complete metric invariant for automorphisms of the torus'', Proceeding of the National Academy of Sciences. '''57''' (1967), 1573–1576.
